lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eEn el \u003cb\u003epi:
"

In pyrrole, furan and thiophene the heteroatom contributes a pair to the π sextet (p orbital, perpendicular to the ring). In pyridine the N already contributes one e⁻ to the π system and its pair stays in the plane (sp²), pointing outward. That difference decides basicity and reactivity.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eLa piridina (pKaH \u0:
"

Pyridine (pKaH 5.2) and imidazole (7.0) are protonated at their in-plane pair. Pyrrole (pKaH ≈ −3.8) is not: protonating the N would destroy the aromaticity. That is why the imidazole of histidine acts as a physiological buffer and is an active site of enzymes. Look at the pKaH graph.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eLos heterociclos de 5:
"

5-membered heterocycles are more reactive than benzene (pyrrole ≫ furan > thiophene) and substitute at C2: the intermediate cation has 3 resonance structures (the positive charge is shared all the way to the heteroatom) versus 2 at C3. In pyridine the opposite occurs: it is strongly deactivated and reacts (poorly) at C3, because attack at C2/C4 would put the + charge on N.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eLos heterociclos está:
"

Heterocycles are at the center of biochemistry: imidazole in histidine; indole in tryptophan; pyrimidines (C, T, U) and purines (A, G) in nucleic acids; pyridine in NAD⁺; porphyrin (4 pyrroles) in heme and chlorophyll. Switch heterocycle and check the “Found in” field.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003ePor ser deficiente en:
"

Being electron-deficient, pyridine undergoes nucleophilic substitution at C2/C4 (e.g. Chichibabin amination with NaNH₂), where the negative charge of the intermediate can sit on N. To facilitate SEAr the N-oxide is used, which donates density to the ring.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eUn \u003cb\u003eheter:
"

An aromatic heterocycle contains at least one atom other than carbon (N, O, S) in a planar ring with 6 π electrons. They are numbered from the heteroatom (position 1). The most common: pyrrole, furan, thiophene (5-membered), pyridine, pyrimidine (6) and imidazole (5, two N). Choose one in the panel.

"
